c: Philadelphia July 10 1784 Regarding circumstance altogether impossible should, smallest degree, incurred displeasure dearest friend – presume again address belief last letter miscarried became one first cares communicate arrival you, dear General, detail occurrence voyages stay England – progress mercantile pursuits, hitherto favored best expectations – flattering prospects continued, think permitted hope supreme happiness one day demonstrating, degree however short goodness, perfect indelible sense gratitude impressed. Agreeably plan acquainted left Princeton – went England auspices M r Morris's introduction – extremely favored M r Simpson's personal friendship London – mediums formed necessary connections, attained every facility whi[ch] pleased complete commercial [objects] – done, having passed time friends, [undecipherable] fortunate happy finding well, embarked London part merchandise month April, arrived Phil[adelphia] speedy agreeable passage – having two voyages forty three days – 19 24 home. Since return, remainder goods arrived, commenced Merchant – sales good, will, hope, continued. ——— M r Morris proved generous friendship, without smallest ostentation obliging – M r Bingham's conduct towards me, England, ever command gratitude, affection, respect – Colonel Wadsworth, likewise London, friendly offers – friends here good indeed. Reflecting, ever shall do, dear General, advantages derived either immediately, little, friendship honored – persuaded change circumstance whether fortunate otherwise, ever rape loved re- membrance goodness – prosperity cherish proudest boast – adversity fortune, reflection merited friendship, administer heartfelt consolation. hope dear M r Lincoln amiable family continue enjoy every blessing flow Virtue health – permit one loves reveres present best wishes, offer every service capable – believe wishes gratefully sincere justly due. situation capacitate execution commands quarter – hope fail favor – confer pleasure, performed punctuality – pleased address Mayor Bolfon – two others name trade here beg leave trouble dear General, best love D r & Mayles – respects Col o & Miss Crafts family – M r Gore – M r M rs Hill, M r S. c: James Monroe Joseph Carleton Trenton Novr. 26. 1784. Dear Sir, favor'd yours 12th days since. thoroughly acquainted sentiments arrang'ments shod. adopted Annapolis ultimately carried. anxious shod. entirely disarm ourselves & leave military affairs union, command ordinance & stores afloat, present situation alone wod. determine conduct. posts certainly evacuated & addition appriz'd Canada, trip took, during recess Congress, commanding officer recd. order hold them, consequence wh. put vessels commission wh. laid aside provisional treaty, upon lakes Erie, Ontario & Champlain. ft. Erie, niagra, & post St. Lawrence far Montreal & saw step wh. argued disposition evacuate posts within bounds, contrary disposition existed Ct. London fully impress'd necessity, view country keeping posts lakes; upon alone direction conduct Indians & fur trade depend. power avail ourselves advantages shut eyes agnst. measures wh. point necessity; loose present moment shall loose ourselves add resources Brith. province Canada. Upon Missisippi, attention call'd conduct Spn., stimulating Indiians agnst. us & hear deny us right navigation. situation, every view, requires wisest arrangement affairs every department, particularly incumbent us yr. department attended to. be, six states, among first objects Congress. cannot determine course Congress pursue, opinion yr. presence shod. immediately requir'd here. say light present consider'd, shod. suppose certainly command, rather, service States; rest assur'd last Congress, & satisfied same, entertain'd high sense merit & services & happy give honorable testimonials it. Believe shall pleasure seek opportunity serve you, doingn thoroughly persuaded time, especially present state affrs., rendering service country. great respect & esteem dear Sir friend & servant, Jas. Monroe

t: Resignation of Brigadier General James Wilkinson
s: "Wilkinson submits his resignation as Brigadier General of the Pennsylvania militia and recommends his successor.\r\n\r\n[ Gen. James Wilkinson to Pre
c: [ Gen. James Wilkinson Pres. Dickinson, 1784 ] Sir, shall offer apology address; doubtless unexpected, occasion will, flatter myself, excuse it. Being long leave State Pennsylvania, conceive duty abdicate Offices Brigadier & Adjutant General, hold militia; sorry cannot observe ceremony inclosing Commissions, present within reach:--And motive Application Interest welfare meritorious, respectable part Society, late Military America; prompted principle & sympathy promote prosperity every proper occasion, every consistent means Power. present return Election Fayette County, Major John Harden stands second Sheriff's Office; permit briefly state Excellency man's merit, without detracting Competitor.--Mr. Harden served alert Army Generals (then Colonels) Morgan & Butler, Northern Campaign, 1777. Rank Lieutenant, can, Adjutant General Army General Gates, assert exposed danger, encountered greater Fatigue, performed real service Officer Station; Parties never exceeding 20 Men, Course Campaign upwards 60 Prisoners, Personal Encounter rear Enemie's position, killed Mohawk [express?], brought dispatches conveying Gen'l Burgoyne Commanding Officer Ticonderoga, loss (indeed) Lock Hair Indian's Fire carried away. sufficient me, Sir, testify merits, Justice characterizes administration rest. honor be, highest respect, excellency's Obedient & Humble Servant, James Wilkinson [Directed] Excellency John Dickinson, Esqr., Philadel'a.

t: Account of the Voyage to China
s: This is Shaw's account of his voyage to China and his encounters with the Chinese people, often contentious, after his arrival in that country.
c: [1785, 19] YORK FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 2. following letter Mr. JAY, Mr. SHAW, went ship Empress China, Canton, commercial agent owners. contains interesting written account voyage. gentleman served United States, during late war, Captain American army; conduct character, acquired confidence esteem Major General Knox, became Aid de Camp brave distinguished officer. NEW-YORK, 19 May, 1785. "SIR, "The first vessel fitted inhabitants United States America, essaying commerce Empire China, being favor Heaven, safe returned port, becomes duty communicate you, information Fathers Country, account reception citizens met with, respect flag treated distant region; especially circumstances occurred, tendency attract attention Chinese towards people hitherto confused ideas, served, peculiar manner, place Americans conspicuous point view, commonly attended introduction nations ancient extensive empire. "The ship employed occasion, three hundred sixty tons burthen, built America, equipped forty three persons, command John Green, Esq. subscriber honor being appointed agent commerce, gentlemen whose risque first experiment undertaken. 22nd February, 1784, ship sailed New-York, arrived 21st March S[ao?] Jago, principal Cape Verd islands. Having paid respects Portuguese Viceroy, permission taken refreshments necessary, left islands 27th, pursued voyage. pleasant passage, nothing extraordinary occurred, came anchor streights Sunda 18th July. small addition happiness occasion, meet two ships belonging good allies French. Commodore, Monsieur D'Ordilen, officers, welcomed us affectionate manner; ship immediately bound Canton, gave us invitation go company him. friendly offer cheerfully accepted, Commodore furnished us signals day night, added instructions passage thro' Chinese seas, extremely beneficial, unfortunate accident occasioned separation. Happily pursued route together. arrival island Macao, French Consul China, Monsieur Vieillard, gentlemen nation, came board congratulate welcome us part world, kindly undertook introduction Americans Portuguese Governor. little time there, entirely taken good offices Consul, gentlemen nation, Sweeds Imperialists, remained Macao. Europeans repaired Canton. Three days afterwards finished outward bound voyage. Previous coming anchor, saluted shipping river thirteen guns, answered several Commodores European nations, sent officer compliment us arrival. visits returned Captain Supercargoes, afternoon; again saluted respective ships, finished visit. French sent officers congratulate us, added obligations ^already them, furnishing men, boats, anchors, assist us coming safe convenient moorings. good offices stop there; furnished us part banksail, insisted ^further until settled, quarters Canton. day arrival Canton, August 30, two following days, visited Chinese merchants, chiefs gentlemen several European establishments:----The Chinese indulgent towards us; stiled us People; map conveyed idea extent country, present increasing population, highly pleased prospect considerable market productions their's. situation Europeans Canton known render detail unnecessary. good understanding commonly subsisting Chinese, degree interrupted two extraordinary occurrences, will, permission, give particular account. "The Police Canton, times extremely strict, Europeans residing virtually circumscribed within narrow limits. latter observed concern circumstances deemed encroachment upon rights. consideration determined apply redress Hoppo, head officer customs, next time visit shipping. Deputies accordingly attended every nation, desired represent our's. met Hoppo board English ship, causes complaint soon removed. "The occurrence beg leave notice, gave rise commonly called Canton War, threatened productive serious consequences. 25th November English ship, saluting company dined board, killed Chinese, wounded two others Mandarine's boat along-side. maxim Chinese law, blood answer blood; pursuance demanded unfortunate Gunner. give poor man, consign certain death-- Humanity pleaded powerfully against measure. repeated conferences English Chinese, latter declared themselves satisfied, affair supposed entirely settled. Notwithstanding this, morning last conference (the 27th) Supercargoe ship seized attending business, thrown sedan chair, hurried city, committed prison. "Such outrage personal liberty spread general alarm; Europeans unanimously agreed send boats, armed men shipping, security themselves property, until matter brought conclusion. boats accordingly came, ours among number, one fired man wounded. trade stopped, Chinese men war drawn opposite Factories. Europeans demanded restoration Mr. Smith, Chinese refused, until Gunner given up. mean while, troops province collecting neighborhood Canton--the Chinese servants ordered Magistrates leave Factories--the gates suburbs shut--all intercourse end--the naval force encreased--many troops embarked boats, ready landing--and every thing wore appearance war. extremities matters might carried, negociation taken place, one say. Chinese asked conference nations, except English. deputation, (in included America) met Fuen, head Magistrate Canton, principal officers province. setting forth, interpreter, power Emperor, determination support laws, demanded Gunner given within three days, declaring impartial examination tribunal, appeared affair accidental, released unhurt. mean time gave permission trade, (excepting English) go usual, dismissed us present two pieces silk each, mark friendly disposition. nations one another, sent away boats protection Chinese flag, pursued business before. English obliged submit--the Gunner given up--Mr. Smith released--and English, being forced ask pardon Magistracy Canton, commerce restored. occasion, happy last sent boat, without Chinese flag; go till English themselves thanked us concurrence them, advised sending away. peace restored, Chief four English gentlemen visited several nations (among included) thanked assistance during troubles--the Gunner remained Chinese, fate undetermined. "Notwithstanding treatment received parties perfectly civil respectful peculiar satisfaction experienced, every occasion good allies French, flattering substantial proofs friendship. "If, they, instance serviceable you, happy,--and desire nothing ardently further opportunities convince affection." "We left Canton, 27th December, return, refreshed Cape Good Hope, found friendly reception--after remaining five days, sailed America, arrived port 11th instant. "To every lover country, immediately concerned commerce, pleasing reflection, communication thus happily opened us Eastern extreme globe; adds sensibly pleasure reflection, voyage performed short space time attended loss one man. Captain Green officers every commendation due, unwearied successful endeavors bringing fortunate issue, fully justifies confidence reposed them, gentlemen concerned enterprize. "Permit me, Sir, accompany letter two pieces silk presented Fuen Canton, mark good disposition towards American nation. view consider myself peculiarly honored being charged testimony friendship Chinese people, years prosecute commerce subjects empire, advantages equal superior enjoyed nation whatever. "I honor be, perfect respect, Sir, obedient, humble servant, Samuel Shaw" Honorable Minister United States Foreign Affairs [1785, 19] YORK FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 2 following letter Mr. JAY, Mr. SHAW, went ship Empress China, Canton, commercial agent owners. contains interesting written account voyage. gentleman served United States, during late war, Captain American army; conduct character, acquired confidence esteem Major General Knox, became Aid de Camp brave distinguished officer. t: Land Ordinance of 1785 for ascertaining the mode of disposing Lands in the Western territory
s: "Congress publishes the Land Ordinance of 1785 on 20 May.  Congress issues guidance for the marking, mapping, subdivision, and sale lands in the weste
c: Ordinance ascertaining mode disposing Lands Western Territory. ordained United States Congress assembled, territory ceded individual States United States, purchased Indian inhabitants, shall disposed following manner: . . . Surveyors, respectively qualified, shall proceed divide territory townships six miles square, lines running due north south, others crossing right angles, near . . . lines shall measured chain; shall plainly marked chaps trees exactly described plat; whereon shall noted surveyor, proper distances, mines, salt springs, salt licks mill seats, shall come knowledge, water courses, mountains remarkable permanent things, near lines shall pass, quality lands . . . board treasury shall transmit copy original plats, previously noting thereon, townships, fractional parts townships, shall fallen several states, distribution aforesaid, Commissioners loan office several states, who, giving notice less two six months causing advertisements posted court houses, noted places every county, inserted one newspaper, published states residence respectively, shall proceed sell townships, fractional parts townships, public venue . . . t: Alarming Report from the Miami
s: Reports alarming intelligence he has received from Capt. Finney at the Miami River on the activities of Indians operating from forts in America's west
c: Philadelphia, 7, 1786 Sir:-, received enclosed letters Captain Finney Miami. intelligence truly alarming, notwithstanding fair reports Commissioners concerning peaceful disposition Indians, convinced treaties farcical, long British posses posts. party Indians alluded letter reconnoitering party Detroit, discovered Captain Strong near garrison McIntosh. Upon party being sent out, fled, being twenty number. Duncan Wilson's reports inclosed, contain reflections General Butler, particularly mentioning small influences among different tribes Indians. wish see them, shall enclose per next opportunity. obedient Servant Jos Harmar General Knox, Sec'y War Philadelphia, 7. 1786. John Johnson (who there) invited six nations to. Moravian Indians (among Bull witoo) learn, even friendly United States. am, obedient servant Jos. t: Describes Territory, People, Indians Surrounding Kaskaskia
s: 'Reports a fatiguing march with Ensign McDowell, 30 men, and 2 Indians: Pachan, a Miami chief, and his commande, who hunted and supplied the company w
c: Kaskaskia, November 24, 1787 Sir: -- marched 9th August post (Vincennes) subaltern, Ensign McDowell, thirty men, prairies, arrived Kaskaskia 16th month. march fatigueing, weather excessively warm, water bad scarce route. distance one hundred eighty sixty miles; French call eighty leagues. accompanied two Indians, (Pachan, Miami Chief Comrade) hunted supplied party meat (buffalo & deer) [editor's note: author crossed undecipherable word] march upon return. prairies extensive, natural meadows, covered long grass; one particular, crossed, eight leagues breadth. run general, North South, like Ocean, far eye see, view terminated horison. Here copse wood interspersed. free brush underwood, least vestige ever having cultivated. country excellent grazing, abounds [editor's note: author crossed undecipherable word] buffalo, deer, bear &c. matter speculation account formation prairies. western side Wabash overflown Spring, several miles. 17th, visited Magistrate prin- -cipal habitants Kaskaskia, welcoming us upon arrival. Baptiste De Coigne, Chief Kaskaskia Indians, paid visit afternoon, delivered speech expressive greatest friendship United States; time presented one Calumets pipes peace, sent on. Peoria Indians likewise visited me. Kaskasias, Peorias, Cahokia Mitchi tribes compare Illinois Indians. almost extinct present, exceeding forty fifty, Total. Kaskaskia handsome little village, situated river name, empties Mississippi two leagues distant it. one hundred five miles mouth Ohio; situation low unhealthy, subject inun- -dation. inhabitants French, much class Post Vincennes; number one hundred ninety one, men young. Having little time spare, left Lieutenant McDowell party Kaskaskia, 18th set out, accompanied Mr Tardiveau gentleman village Cahokia. gained Prairie Du Rocher, small village five french leagues Kaskaskia, halted night. 19th passed St. Philip, trifling village three leagues distant Prairie Du Rocher, dined La Bellefontaine, six leagues further. t: Public notification of legal boundary with Cherokee Nation
s: Public notice of treaty with the Cherokee Nation.
c: United States Congress Assembled. PROCLAMATION. WHEREAS United States Congress assembled, Commissioners duly appointed authorized, twenty-eighth Day November, One Thousand Seven Hundred Eighty-five, Hopewell, Keowee, conclude Articles Treaty Cherokees; among things stipulated agreed, Article fourth, "That Boundary allotted Cherokees hunting Grounds, Indians Citizens United States, within limits United States America, shall following, viz." Beginning mouth Duck River Tennessee; thence running Northerly along waters running Cumberland running Tenehe; thence Eastwardly along ridge north-east line run, shall strike South-Holston thirty-eight miles above Nashville; thence along line river; thence river fork Kentucky road cuts river; thence Campbell's line near Cumberland Gap; thence mouth Cloud's Creek Holstein; thence Chimney-Top Mountain; thence Cany Creek, near mouth Big Lime Stone Nolichuckey; thence Southerly course six miles mountain; thence South North-Carolina line; thence South-Carolina Indian Boundary; forth South-West top Oconee Mountain, till shall strike Tugelo river; thence direct line top Currahoe Mountain; thence head South fork Oconee river." Article fifth, "If Citizen United States, person being Indian, attempt settle lands within and/or South Boundary, allotted Indians Hunting Grounds, having settled prior conclusion Treaty, removing within six months ratification Treaty, person forfeit protection United States, Indians might punish law please:" provided, fifth Article construed exclude settled fork French Broad Holstein rivers, whose particular situation transmitted United States Congress assembled decision thereon, Indians agreed abide by." whereas represented Congress, several Persons settled Frontier North-Carolina, vicinity Chota, have, open violation Treaty, intrusions upon Indian Hunting Grounds, committed many unprovoked outrages upon Cherokees, Treaty put themselves protection United States, proceedings highly injurious disrespectful authority Union, being firm determination Congress protect Cherokees rights, according true intent meaning Treaty: UNITED STATES CONGRESS ASSEMBLED, therefore thought fit issue, hereby issue Proclamation, restrain Persons unconstitutional intrusions, forbid proceeding against Cherokees, enjoining settled upon Hunting Grounds Cherokees, depart Families Effects within time, shall think proper, determination expressed Resolution peril: Provided, Proclamation shall construed requiring removal People settled fork French Broad Holstein rivers, referred Treaty: Provided also, nothing contained Proclamation shall considered affecting Territorial Claims State North-Carolina. DONE Congress, First Day September, Year Lord One Thousand Seven Hundred Eighty-eight, Sovereignty Independence Thirteenth. CYRUS GRIFFIN, President. CHARLES THOMSON, Secretary.

s: Document, report describes the Creek country, people, culture, and government. Refers to horse theft and trials.
c: Philadelphia 2d. 1791. [centered] honorable Henry Knox Esquire-- Secretary department war. Sir. Persuant letter instruction, honor receive 18th August 1791.-- accompanied Brigr. Generl. McGillivray, Chiefs warriors Creek nation, attended treaty New-York, place, Nation.-- Fortunately disaster happened voyage St. Marys river, Journey land Country, occasioned use authority pleased give drawing you, case found necessary.---- arrived safe first indian villages Flint River, latter part September. Situated found myself among people, inclination, found interest, become useful possible Great Chief; occasions endeavoured impress Jealous Minds indians general, White people United States, Sincere candid overtures peace friendship towards them: being myself power, pledged them, truth told them, friends, witnesses great White Town. conceived Genl McGillivray viewed time, rather light spy, otherwise.-- uniform declaration contrary, persevering attention person, flattered suspicions removed, alteration conduct towards me, reason believe gained Confidence effectually. found experiment, learn language, pronounce well, task Several Youthful years--therefore obtaining vocabulary principal words, fameliar sentences, directed enquiries particularly objects contained letter. making notes country, found myself watched eye Jealousy, therefore thought pru= dent keep sight, always did, even friend Mr. McGillivray himself. Going country, down southern corner it-- traveling Chatahoosee river Coweta district-- thence crossing country westward Little-Tallassie:-- coming it, route districts tribes upper Creeks, Natches.-- Together variety jaunts visits, different Towns villages Coosades Alabamas.-- one general meeting Tuckabatches.-- residing Little Tallassie; afforded comprehensive view whole country lower upper Creeks, oppertunity seeing largest Villages, becoming generally known among them. following sheets contain result observations during excursion, humbly beg leave honor, offering you, hope, contain information, respect Natives fine country possess, pleasing satisfactory yourself, interesting useful Government. |4.| [centered] attached indians, manner living, once sacrificing social virtues, disgusting habits Savage barbarism. custom McGillivray spend winters sea Coast among Spaniards, leaving wife, servants, horses, plantation near Tensau, within border West Florida, 180 Miles down Albama River, Returning pass summer nation: therefore could remained Country, winter season, without suffering inconvenience Cold, probably hunger, without companion. Sir, reasons induced leave Country soon, presume, whoever try experiment longer time done, find sufficient exercise [strike through, illegible, blot] patience, fortitude, solitary Philosophy. [following text roughly centered page] honor perfect venerat= ion respect. Sir, devoted obedient Humble Servant Caleb Swan depy. agent Creek Nation-- [elaborate scroll] |5.| [centered] Journal -- Transcript, abridged. August 19th 1790 Sailed York B General Mc. Gillivray indian Chiefs, bound St Marys river. September -- 1st-- Captain Smith Schooner in, imprudently, run vessel large breaker North end Cumberland Island-- vessel struck several times sand, afterwards went over. 2nd Arrived save Captain Burbecks post mouth St Marys, received visit compliment Dr. Charles Caxton Howard & Others, East Florida. 8nd Proceeded head river, remained three days Mr. Marburys procuring horses-- here Several Chiefs lower towns, separated pursued routes homeward. Sept. 11. Took departure Spanish Creek head St. Marys. Sept. 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. 17. 18. 19 & 20. incessant rains, five horses died way. 21. Came Alabaha, branch river St. Marks, found flooded, half mile banks side; pro= pects gloomy. provisions mostly waisted spoiled, late rains, Journey stopped floods. 22d. Endeavoured build canoe, having small hatchet, attempt fruitless. 23d. waters continued rise. 24th waters Stand. 25th indians killed Stray cow woods Stretched ^her Skin, hoops, Shape bowl, experiment getting over. 26th. Early morning indians commenced swiming, towing Skin boat-- Setting war-hoop frighten away Alegators, here vast numbers.-- uncomman hazardous exertion, were, baggage Safe dark, having met accident except loss four horses, entangled drowned swiming river. 27.th__ Supplied ourselves 15 fresh horses, taken Jack Kinnards Negroes, met woods, bound St Marys horses sale. 30th Arrived Chehan towns flint river, found indians assembled great numbers hear news Chief given lost. October 1. encamped John Kinnards borders lower Creeks & Seminolies fresh supply provisions. October 5th Crossed Chattahoosee river broken arrow 12 miles below Cussitah Cowetas Towns. 7th Crossed Tallapossie river Tuckabatches-- here Chief Communications people, assembled hear talk. 8th-- Arrived Little Tallassie Alabama river._____ 20th Attended general meeting, called mad dog King Tuckabatches, McGillivray further communications people-- seemd pleased, others threw tobacco fire disgust. 21. snow fell inch deep Country 22nd Moon totally eclipsed, served regulate account time, variety causes, able Keep accurately. Note-- Indians surrounding Villages yelling fear, firing Guns every direction.-- |8.| [centered] opinion, occasions, large frog swallowing Moon, hideous noises frighten away. Oct. 29. Mrs. Mc Gillivrays sister, hanged herself passion, cut down & Saved. November 20th-- -- woman related McGillivray, hanged herself Tuskeegee town, Little Tallasie, privately buried village evening. 27.th Charles Weatherford brought letter Secretary War, dated 15. Sept. 1790. December. 15th left Little Tallassie, upper country arrived Natchez Villages two days. 20th. Went Mountains district Hillabes. December 21. Arrived Ufalas; attended square, three times black drinks; pressing invitation White Lieutenant. Note-- white Lieutenant half breed. Great war Mico district oakfuskies point appearance |9) [centered] abilities, rival Chief Country. 50 years age, 6 feet 2 inches high made, sole influence 1000 gun-men. 22nd. Crossed Chatahoosa, upper war path horse-ford 60 miles above Cussitahs Cowetas. 24th Crossed flint river upper falls, Stretched down country south East direction. Decemeber 27.th Crossed Oakmulgee river falls middle trading path. Note---- lands, path, indian villages, Chattahoosee river, eastward Oakmulgee, even Ocoonee rivers, superior quality.-- might give pain traveller view it, rude desart, little labor might "blossom like rose." 28th. [centered] St Marys River crooked, |10.| [centered] wide open Marsh side, mouth upward ofor 30 miles; marsh terminated thick woods, river becomes nearly straight 30 miles further Allens, indian trader head navigation. trading station, river like dead Creek, 4 fathoms deep 10 Rods wide. laid down Reved. Alabaha, laid down common maps southern country; considerable river; 100 Miles west head St Marys running southerly direction: often difficult crossed, banks (11.) t: Disposition of the Indians in This Quarter
s: Reverend Kirkland reports on sundry councils with representatives of the western tribes and assesses the prospects for peace or war on the frontier.
c: Genl Knox Kanawages Febry 13 1792 No.l Kanawageas 13th Febr7 1792 Sir came here night last, honor addressing 6 insth place - informed dispatched two Runners Buffaloe, adapted speech Good Peter & chiefs hasten proposed delegation season far advanced. express, Viz Capt Hendrick & French Peter, hoped entertaining obtaining necessary & much desired information proceedings lst Indian Council holding wch white person could admitted. Since last variety occurrences taken place, turned things Tuesday last rode down here meet Red Jacket & another Buffaloe Chief - informed Farmers Brother, proceed directly Buffaloe designed parted Genesee - spent several days conference him, hunting quarters - & sent Compliments me, assuring ift return Genesee - wished exercise little patience. - Red Jacket acquainted report story propagated young mohawk came Buffaloe company trader tht quarter & employed him. told heard last evening. prospect story this. Chiefs Buffaloe & Grand River several weeks private council Niagare - & determined send representation Congress [undecipherable] Capt. Pickerings invitation & suffer go - next Council held Grand River, western Indians present!! Invited Red Jacket & Buffaloe chief visit Genesee & conference Good Peter immediately returned Genesee. Wednesd--morng--sent express Red Jacket lest come & convince number Seneka Chiefs & head warriors Good Peters advice inquire mohawks report. - found came authority - broke - eveng - came first Runner -- Capt John surprize returned Capt Hendrick & good French Peter - Capt Hendricks instructions pointedly proceed, till actually met Chiefs whether way down - council te Buffaloe - Niagare - & know delayed them, & find measures adopted private council. However reason assigned returning Capt John (whom met 30 miles side Buffaloe) purport message Farmers Brother even arrival - follows. "Brother, return Capt Pickering, Council fire Genesee - & inform Councillors & warriors waiting, Chiefs return Niagare where, council Capt Butler three weeks, & ready set Genesee within three Days - soon start shall send Runner, notify certify numbers - & day shall arrive. time far elapsed whole Delegation Genesee themselves ready, & meet us Village called Kanawageas, short interview & [boding?] Congress [indecipherable] shall proceed set together & possible speed persue journey great Council 13-us. - & hear say us." three strings wampum cordial salutation bring te [messages?] Farmer Brothr. message seemed diffuse universal joy - good Peter having ox killed occasion. proposed defering it, till runner arrive anouncing having actually set numbers asertained! agreed to. Notified general council next morng 10 o'clock Indians collected. 10 - Thursday 10 o'clock. came two Senekas, message Great Sky & Capt. Brant directly Niaga message recd hands Runner Kanawageas [indecipherable] proceed two Belt purport follows - "that great Sky (the Onondaga Chief) summoned council Buffaloe Creek, give particular instruction representatives Nation might think best attend Coll Pickerings repeated Invitations, visit Congress - named ten Seneka Chiefs Genesee & vicinity whose immediate attendance required - large belt - second message - "capt. Brant sends compliments friend Mr Kirkland. immediate representative Coll Pickering superendt Ind aff. & invites come Council Buffaloe Creek" -- small Belt -- declared, Runner come three days Niagara -- ye term three sleeps - three nights including preceding & succeeding days - much doubted present depth snow [undecipherable] travelling second message much changed face things one bro't Oneida Runner, Capt John evening - & seemed spread gloom almost every countenance - hour chiefs & head warriors, Senekas assembled council house - together delegation Oneidas, onondgas & Cayugas. Good Peter opened council introductory speech - [indecipherable] followed. name, cautiously wording fixed opinion upon subject us. name addressed whole council masterly stile & bringing view practice & usages Fathers, difference opinion subsisting upon important matter wch concerned weal whole - & advised great deliberation upon two respective different messages lay them, importing direclty opposite measures. - Red Jacket next spoke - & displayed genius ing abilities eloquence engaging manner - & gave decidedly opinion contrary questions & asuages [editors note: father ?], remove, extinguish one council fire, calling another, till design & intent first attended to, decided upon place appointed. - superintendt Indian affairs Congress, appointed Genesee, place, rendayvous, meeting, Six nations, concerned treaty Newtown, meet, & prepare instruction 2. might think necesarry, representatives, invited Congress--[undecipherable] order give Congress opportunity confer them, & fulfill voluntary engagements, & promisses superintendant Coll. Pickering treaty Newtown last summer.-- further offered, present warrior force sometime kindled River--& things ready go foreward, waiting delegation Buffaloe sufficiently [undecipherable] notified & subsequent council [undecipherable], custom [undecipherable] [fathom?] supercede this, till subject here fairly decided upon--if substantial imaginary objections [undecipherable] mind sort [undecipherable] against pro proposals supernt Indn affairs confederacy Congress, Let here place appointed fair & candid hearing.-- apparent, design being called Buffaloe, instruction--was extinguish Council here,--& delay fusiness till, season ws far advanced--they could perform journey--Indeed-it opinion & [undecipherable] presumed obvious everyone--that real design Great Skye's message [undecipherable] attempt prevent representation five nation going Congress all--the message itself spoke [undecipherable] free declare opinion full council--even presence Onondaga chiefs Brother's Tribe-. say, without reflecting upon Nation-at large, profound unprecedented, one single man, Onondaga Nation summon council--& call ten chiefs & warriors Seneka Nation without single voice nation--. Therefore message Farmer's Brother, thought ought first attended attended to--& finally adheared to.--However, part riske ocdcasion, great [skey?] message upon judgement four Onondaga Chiefs here here present--as Great Skey, Great Skey &c one nations." house consultation--the Onondagoes reply unanimously favour first message--The reasonings upon subject cannot relate justice say spoke friendly terms highest respect & respectful manner Americans--its allied confederated Brother--& expresssed firm & unlimited confidence Congres---Ther speech near hour length.- Good Peter & Red Jacket int heir turnj displayed oritorical geniuses--I scarse ever entertained Indian Council--. persuaded even commanded attention afforded [entertained?] present. 10 o'clock evening. whole Council unanimously agreed replied paying [undecipherable] respect Coll Pickerings message Superintendt & affair [undecpherable] annuity even Presidt n agreeable ancient messages six nations, extinguish council fire kindled burning Genesee, & repair one called kindled Buffaloe, till business former properly settled.--& division place difference opinion Lat subsist--Let Chiefs Buffaloe watch council fire appear there, others go Congress pursuit object, object view asame--and two best Runners sent next day--with answer great sky, time, inviting gentle persuasive & friendly manner repair Genesee, & adjusting affairs.--And Mr Kirkland, Father, left option making reply message friend Capt Brant. 10 o'clock eveng adjourned--& proposed meet again next morning & very--particularly instruct Runners--who already chosen--Viz one Onondaga & one Seneka.-- mean conferred Good Peter & Red Jacket upon subject answer Capt Brant--. soon found unwilling go leave them--at present, opinion--that return answer similar theirs, & wait return Runners. went away considered Indians Congress council fire (as stile it) extinguished--which weaken cause--& leave [undecipherable] here & [undecipherable] [undecipherable] give Buffaloes occasion triumph & put every advantage hands. left situation force [reconfering?] & [undecipherable] adhere [undecipherable] advice advice--as tho' strong inclination send back belt mild, con set [undecipherable] interview friend Capt. Brant. proposed paid privately, whether might send friend mine, & particular friend Capt Brants--to meet Buffalo stead condition come there. Friend proposed Genl Chapin.--They consented gratify me--but spoken public council--as sink dignity Council fire kindled River order Congress.-- Friday--morn 9-10 o'clock--The Indians again assembled Council house--Good Peter open Council mos masterly speech upon maxims & customs forefathers--particularly difference opinion subsisted Confederacy nations. mild, soft & persuasive manner address carried him. transactions yesterday [rehearded?] over--examined & corrected wanted appeared deficiency.-- two o'clock PM--the two Runners, having recd instructions, set Buffaloe--& return practicable, five six sleeps farthest."--we sat council till 9 o'clock eveng--after this. Senekas visit quarters including & tarried till late. & obliged set write ab[out?][undecipherable] insight Good Peter & Red Jacket become sociable other.-- 3 3.-- almost like hand & glove.-- Thus far wrtoe--Journal-wise--that better comprehensive idea situation & disposition Indians quarter: number invialably strongly attached interest united States-- & complexion opinion division six Nations soon place unless accommodation sd bro't about. British interest, apprehensive same, & therefore wage importance union among themselves--. Power including Kayaghsoteas & Cornplanter [undecipherable] Allegany contain nearly two thirds three quarters Seneka Nation--. buffaloe--including Cayoga's & Onondagas--in connection grand--River, form respectable part confederacy--& local circumstances form receive first application western tribes Indians--& ready access them; gives might importance Buffaloe settements &c Grand river--and this, characters, men grand influence ability distinguished---Viz-Fishcarrier, great skye--Farmer's Brother--Little Billy--[undecipherable] young [quarter?] [& house?] man & Brant, weight rest.--we Good Peter--Cornplanter, & Red Jacket & Little Beard--who equal abilities abilities & influence forementioned ex Capt. Brant excepted.-- inclined think farmers Brother, & Little Billey, bro't American interest. Saturday 11th Febry 1,o'clock PM--Dr Allen returned, sent express Niagare, returned letter Capt Brant--after perusing letter & conversation passed betwixt us, desired him, return evening, much fatigued Kanawageus--where appointed meet Genl Chapin--on business--& told first go Jonee's & felt enough--would meet place & time desired--The Chiefs gone Tuscarora Village perform ceremony condolence Aghshegwalesers, Tuscarora Chief--who lately lost relation--This detained till sunset--that near nine o'clock reached Kanawageas--. met Genl Chapin--for sent forby express--But unwell myself could attend little, till last evening--Genl Chapin opinion present, leave Indians, means, lose influence River--& able himself undertake journey trip Buffalo.--But Runners came back Buffaloe, either go, condition thought could endure journey--or stay here, & keep council fire Genesee, absent, tour, go Buffaloe Buffaloe.-- Now, Sir,, please permit observations present complexion affairs & measures taken future honor U.S. & peace frontiers. First.--From communications upon present state Indians quarter--& throughout whole Six Nations--It probable division soon place among them, unless general peace settled Indians.--They begin already sides.--five Tuscaroras marched Saturday last--for settlement near landing place below falls Niagare, & determination return, unless Capt Brant advise them. Buffaloe--previous setting out--the former strenuously insist immediate compliance Coll P.' invitation. Secondly--I obtain respectable & proceed accordingly Representation sachems & head warriors River & Eastward repair Congress & Buffaloes decline & shall insist gerneral council & query, whether doing justice, insist general council Buffaloe, previous setting deny them? whether good policy go without farmers Brother & Little Billy loth go [undecipherable] Fr Br. & Little Billey, two, (including Red Jacket) already engaged, effectual check upon settlements Buffaloe--Cayugas excepted--.-- Thirdly, fail taking down respectable representation five nations Congress & Indian war carried ensuing season--Tis opinion, great majority young warriors men whole five nations active western Indians--the Oneidas excepted. young warriors Buffaloe & grand River (a excepted) look envy upon victory laurels feathered head, & regret, having action Past fall Miami-- Capt Brant himself declared Dr Allen 36 men including 12 Cayugas & Senekas, went without action--all returned unhurt, plunder--& man scalp--; went without Brants approbation, & contrary advice--chose officers & bid defiance Doquanny, Cayuga first Captain.--that situation return Quebeck, 4 4- say much--That young men almost infatuated war, since defeat Army-- [humanly?] speaking--nothing Head warrior calling [persons?]--to desist, & quit persuitg vanquished--prevented whole retreating army being killed, taken man. Capt Brants declaration, universally believed among Indians-- duty inform you, incontestable evidence (stubborn facts) Indians westward--& particularly vicinity Oneida Niagara, been, & plentifully supplied Cloathing--arms & amunition--by British, agents Indian department--& encouraged prosecute war. amount 12000 L1200 [ed: 1200 pounds dollars][undecipherable] distributed Indians Grand River & Buffaloes during Dr Allens short stay Niagara garrison--among considerable number first rate, arms.--but sixpence worth, whole Genesee settlements.-- Fourthly.-should Buffaloes, Grand River--settlements, River, become united--& join western Confederacy--the frontiers state & Pennsylvania, be, apprehension defenseless part & wide extended frontier Unjited States.--a strong garrison prevent which, act established Preskile south side Lake Erie, might afford greatest defense--unless British shall resign western ports--then might soon settled. - suggest idea knowledge country--pardon me, politician--nor politicians son, feel anxious wellfare country. Fifthly enjoin upon me, find result Indian Council Buffaloe--there Council held there, Niagare--& part time--no white person, even Coll Butler himself admitted--which whole garrison Niagare, & Col. Butler himself watch Brant jealous eye.--It sir, next impossible access private councils.--They cannot --or pretend--they cannot, investigate Niagare. following best amt give you--which communicated utmost confidence--by several Indians employed [undecipherable] & different times.--Even good Peter trembled, disclose discovered, lest known, come knowledge it, & life endangered thereby; however much afraid that, private place write.-- "First Shawenes & southern Confederacy since defeat army sent Grand River, Buffaloe, & Canada Indian calling genl Council held miami, early next spring (--probably till waters open--)at time & place every nation, Deputies, declaration whether King--or Americans, Indians distinction two former.-- 2nly--An severe & alarming message sent shawanese Brant mohawks [undecipherable]--in words--"you chief mohawk! doing?--time was, reveled us war, & told us tt Indians join King happy people--& become independent, short time changed voice--& went sleep & left us lurch--. mohawk chief! ruined us.--& shall share us. know good lie longer--arise & bestir yourself!!-- Upon Capt Brant counselled Fish Carrier--great skey--& several others--Three attempts form answer--that might satisfactory--but someone council replied--It satisfactory--upon Brarnt, Fish Carrier replied, could go father;--let matter tried Buffaloe Creek.--In meantime--forbid Indians coming down way--ie. eastward Buffaloe Creek--& one allowed go there, could depended upon.-- Council, Capt Brant proposed first steps taken, immediate healing divisions yt subjecting themselves--+ restoration implicit confidence among one another-- Viz--the division subsisting Grand River betwixt & Capt Aarons party. nextly betwixt & Senekas--& proceede alienation & [jealousy?] Buffaloes & Genesee settlements--that done before, proper answer could given, propriety & safety western Indians."--that representaton go down Congress till union compleated & confidence restored himself difficulty--they help him.-- Lastly.--By Capt Brants letter me, & Dr. Allens, here inclose--there highest probability, Capt Brant immediately come down Congress, proper invitation given.--He person high feelings & knows importance--has & treated confidence first character Great Britain. gentlemen Canada, set plate upon Table Capt Brant, makes entertainment--& one vicinity Niagare, keeps table comprable his.-- Pray, Sir, impropriety illustrious Presidents desiring Coll Pickering even self present complements Capt--Brant & desiring visit purposes inquiring state Indians &c--this effect matter--& doubt thing else b esteem acquisition, ten [symbol pounds]10,000 dollars towards protection frontier. 5 5. & almost believe, might peace western Indians, space eight six eight months. [derange?] plans & alarms once. reason Brant easily detached.--his critical situation western Indians--& dislike Butler & British garrisen Commander Coll Jordon--broke open letter Brant delivered Fish Carrier--& retained two weeks--which company [surcally] trick & teach better.-- Sir, loth quit country without one trial Capt Brant--or least interview him--. shall tarry here, till hear you--indeed, doc Genesee & buffaloe don't agree go down together--If Buffaloe Delegation dont agree come down immediately--The Genesee & representatives determined set Congress--I believe, persuade release & go down Genl Chapin tho disappoinment them. true, Indians give opinion, Brant never come down, tis power congress move him--many white people te sentiment.-- DrKerr--(surgeon Garrison Niagare,) married Capt Brants neice--a natural daughter Sir Wms said, Dr Allen, knows Brant come down properly invited & sorry seen Mr Kirkland. Gentleman & Brant intimate & fond two Brothers.--It apply Governor Clinton Brant spoken rather severe terms him--cant forget Cayoga treat Albany., told Dr Allen-- guilty indecent proposal Presidents [simple?] [undecipherable] Capt Brant [imparte?] weakness, tender concern safety fellow citiznes--& want profoundest respect found Beloved, President, for, God witness, man Earth, venerate respect & esteem equally beloved President. situation things quarter think shall justified hiring express convey letterr--I expect write again course four five days forward without much expense. readily excuse scribbling writing manner writing know destitute almost every convenience--& obliged [undecipherable] end night--lest give umbrage excite jealousy minds Indians--they spies round us among us--& day time continually thronged Indians--wherever go--all inquiring news Congress--what Congress go Indians.--It propagated Buffaloe Creek--that Red Jacket & number others--when Philadelphia, put irons, hanged.-- wrote part last night--& whole this. day dawns--& express soon set out--I ordered go wyoming & return way--may God bless you, & long presume beloved President--&c prays, [undecipherable] Sr--your obedt hum Servt, S. Kirkland Kanawageas Honble Genl Knox PS. like forgot mention tht two 300 dolars wd useful parts shall see fit send Express--James M. Reed.

t: Colonel Pickering address to the Senekas and their Chief mourning the death of Farmer's Brother's Son
s: In this speech, Pickering expresses grief over the death of Farmer's Brother's Son. He says he knew the charming boy and Farmer's Brother took him eve
c: Coll Pickering War Dept Senekas April 1792 Brothers Five Nations. Listen voice United States uttered occasion appointed represent them. Brothers, second time called utter voice grief, loss another member Five Nations--the Son Farmer's Brother--I knew boy: Often taken hand often supplied little wants: charming boy--the darling fond father.--How often witness tender affection?--He carefully lead hand--place knees--and carry arms. Wherever went, little son inseperable companion. viewed pleasure parent's doating fondness--and soft affection child, clinging parent's breast.--But endearments ended; renewed. father return house--he see place little son wont practise harmless sports--and where, weary, used rest.--He look round--but find him.--His grief revive--and again manly cheeks bathed tears.--Brother! [turning Farmers Brother] mourn loss--the loss son--a son lately object fond affection--a son, lived, might staff, support grown old.--But course things earth. herbs spring field: morning fresh green; put forth flowers:--in evening withered dead. trees blossom bring forth fruit, grow, looks fair & ripens: parts soon perish: either tender blossoms, suddenly wither blown away: young, green state drop ground. Brother, presence Great Spirit. You, I, acknowledge superintendency things: and, express it--"we belong him."--and being his, dispose us seemith best. [underline] wisdom [underline] never wanders right way; [underline] goodness [underline] knows bounds. [underline] see little way: [underline] seeth things: [underline] eyes nothing hid. hears speak, knows thoughts hearts: power nothing resist. wisdom, goodness--we rest satisfied satisfied, whether giveth [underline] life [underline], taketh [underline] [underline] away [underline]--all best. Brother, Let considerations afford comfort heart, assuage grief: strings let wipe tears eyes, see eyes brothers here present--that see clearly:--with let open mouths speak--and ears hear; remove every weight breasts, hearts ease; quietly attend important business transact.

t: Regarding the Bowles Affair
s: Knox refers to the treaty McGillivray and chiefs made with the United States in New York. States that Bowles' presence and his absence have been troub
c: [1. P] [Traduccion] Departamento de la Guerra. 20 de Abril de 1792—Muy S. mio recibido con mucho gusto el regreso de Vm esta tailapia — Aunque es satisfactorio tener noticias de Vm. por medio de un tercio si, sin embargo desearía mas que con pecuenacia, y ampliamente escribiere x [undecipherable] en tiempo. El trabajo hecho en Nueva York entre los criados unidos con Vm y los otros Jefes catabuches añade mucho de echoles fundamentos una nueva felicidad para esa Nacion, si de él se hace el uso propio, y conveniente. El fuego entonces encendido se que se le suministre tiempo en tiempo pabulo, para que sea perpetuo La presencia del Impostor Bowles, y la aventura de Vm (supongo en consecuencia de aquellas) ha ocasionado alguna incomodidad, pero felizmente el amor este oficio ha dirigido al Gobio. Espero sinceramente que Vm. arregle inmediatamente sus cosas con M. r Seagrove para fixar las lindeas de los limites conforme al tratado de Nueva York. Un señorío demasiado de la naturaleza humana para permitir que qualquiera de necesaria demora producirá una comodidad en timientes, viendo por tanto al interes de todos se moven, y prevenir todo motivo de mala inteligencia. El sistema que el Presidente de los Estados Unidos, y el Gobierno general han adoptado con respecto los negocios de los Indios esta tan lleno se atenciones ellos, que todo hombre de bien debe deleitarse en promover sus miras. se piden riquezas los Indios, nadie mar se solicita ellos que lo que puede contribuir su felicidad, y propia dicha. M. r Seagrove quien tengo exante exteriormente, explicara Vm. todos, y cada una de las disposiciones del Gobierno para su satisfaccion. Se estan poniendo en execucion todos los medios, que se han juzgado conducentes inducir los Indios al Norueste del Ohio que hagan las paz, y deseamos con ansia que produzcan efecto. Pero si los dichos Indios despues de estar plenamente convencidos de las humanas intenciones de los Estados unidos continuaren sus depredaciones sobre los indefensos frontera aquellos, la misma humanidad deberia un verso contigo. En este, y único conocimiento unas cientos, o docientos guerreros de esa Nacion lo mas se emplearian ventajosamente con nuestro Ejercito. Tenga Vm. la complacencia de observar ante esto: pronto que si esos Indios se unen con nosotros, se juntaran con los Indios enemigos; pero ruego Dios que ni se uno, ni esto Lado sea necesario. M. r Seagrove manifestara Vm. las particulares instrucciones que tiene sobre el asunto. Tengo la satisfaccion de informar Vm. que su sobrino esta bueno, que crece mucho; que aprende con la expedicion que puede Severse, que esta con unido; y que su conducta es irreprehensible, prueba y su aprovechamiento: escribo al Vm. la incluira. Soy Vm Señor, con la mayor atencion, y estima su mas humilde servidor, y amigo. [undecipherable] Secretaro de la Guerra. Señor Brigadier General D. r Alexandre M. r Gillesney. [ψL: Baron de [undecipherable: probable reading Carondelete]]

t: Letter from John Harris, Fort Washington, to Samuel Hodgdon on Indian attacks and expression for support for Hodgdon against slanderous attacks
s: Notes that he heard through General Putnam of Hodgdon's safe arrival at Marrietta. Cavalry arrived from Kentucky; General Wilkinson accompanied them t
c: Letter Jno Harris Fort Washington, July 6th, 1793 Dear Sir happy having opportunity writing you. probable meet pleasing family far remote Janus Discord, Calamity & War. happily informed Genl Putnam safe arrival Marietta, & shall happy hear accident happened place & Philada. one hundred Cavalry arrived Kentucky command Capt. Barbec soon left us. Genl. Wilkinson accompanied Fort Jefferson. 25th last month savages attacked party one Serjeant, one Corporal & twelve, cutting grass prairie adjacent Garrison (Fort Jefferson), every one party cut - three bodies found, much mangled. number Indians supposed sixty & one Hundred. evening 8d instant. Seven Wabash Indians arrived post Mr. Viego, among Bill, [undecipherable] (so called) & largest Boy went Mr. Manard. Mr. Viego informs several parties Indians cross'd Ohio Kentucky. Major Beatty writes opinion; collective forces Savages double last year. expects bloody Autumn. almost beyond doubt Major Freeman & party off: Bill informs (coroborated report Vincennes) Shawonees met Flag Harmer's Trace- five six days travel Fort Washington, fired them, killed three dead spot. person carried Flag kept ground. Indians came & took him, kept minutes & killed him. took papers &c - & carried back Town examination persons understood English. found great Father White Chief & sorry done. Indians seems, collected large Bodies Wabash & Miami Rivers. effects futurity discover. business Department situated usual - Small Escorts & go come. order GenSuperscript textl. Wilkinson purchased waggon & one Hundred Hundred Bushels Salt Capt. Armstrong mowing Hay prairie adjacent Fort Hamilton. Hay - - prepared salt & properly secured think essential service next fall Horses & Oxen. Corn purchased Territory price. Mr. Smith delivered his. Kentucky boats gone. shall shell & bring down Keel-boats. heard complaint part & hope none. determined & everything power indemnify surety. several Combats (viva vou) attempted vindicate issue Truth & Might, against slander Calumny & Malice. Thank God. hold own. dear Sir, altho popular Horizon appears persons slanted - sincerely hope rays sun conscious Bright & Merit dart force souls grovling Slander Reproach cause hide heads & screen themselves open shame. Genl. Putnam command post. means leave us days Fort Jefferson. received Order respecting Indian Goods. shall attentive [taking?] receipts Major Strong desired put mind paper left accepting recruiting business: wishes sent forward first opportunity. sudden departure deprived private conversation you, permit therefore (my dear Sir) tender sincere thanks past favor, pleased confer & hope present & future conduct ensure future interest & Friendship rumored party Indian prisoners & quantity Goods sent post Vincennes Fort Knox - thing official respecting it. good enough Sir present Compliments David Brown - altho unacquainted Family, Thank present best respects Adieu dear Sir, & believe highest sentiment Friendship & Gratitude, Respect & Esteem Obdient Servant, Jno Harris. Samuel Hodgdon Esqr Philadelphia [Letter J. o Harris] Fort Washington, July 6 th 1795 Dear Sir. happy having opportunity writing — probable meet pleasing Family. Prision Domestic felisomy & men — happlily informed Gen l Robinson safe arrivall Princeton, & shall able therefore happly hear accidents happened place & [undecipherable] Nearly five hundred Cavalry arunded Gen l Chanteling near Lower Side — left us. Gen l Wilkinson accompanied Gen l Jefferson — 25 th June Savages indicated Party depredations Surprised — Whites setting traps Priries adjacent Garrison Officers — 385 one Parties cut off, two found — much — number Indians supposed Sixty & one hundred. — Evening 8 th instant Wabash Indians arived Post Mr Boys, among Buck fine — (so called) largest Boy went M c Donalds Mr Boys informs Several Parties Indians urged Ohio Kentucky — Major Beatty writes opinion attentive force Savages double last year. expects bloody Autumn — almost beyond doubt Major Freeman & Party set — Bell informs (corroborated report Vincence) Shawanese met Flag main trace — five six days travel Fort Washington, fired them, Killed three dead spot, Person carried Flag, leapt ground. Indians came & took him, kept minutes & killed him. took Papers & commission back town — examination Person understood English found great Talks White Chief & wrong done — Indians forms, collected large Bodies heads Miami Kitts effect ferocity doubtless — language Department pleased speak — Truth, notice go — order Gen l Wilkinson purchased Negro — Remaked Bandot Seth Clumbring living Prairie adjacent Fort Hamilton Boy — Purchased Dett perfectly found think assistance. Pardon not, trifle thin — Dress here shipped Territory price. Mr Beatts — Particulary Beate found. Shall & bring down bulk — heard complaint hope none — determined & every thing Power accomodate friends. Several long lets (viva voce) attempted combat rage Brother Biggs against Border below Father. Thank God hold — dear Sir, altho fabulous Mission appears Persons abandoned firmly hope, rays Sun conscious Biggs Ment rest force heads groaning Sons Sordid Selfpreservation cause hide heads & absent themselves Shame — Gen l Robinson command Post, means leave us days Fort Jefferson — forward Order respecting Indian goods. shall attentive taking Invoices Major Strong, asked put mind Paper left respecting recruiting Inlistings; wishes put forward first opportunity — sudden departure, deprived private consultation you. Permit therefore — now, dear Sir, tender sincere thanks, kind favors, Pleased confer me. & hope Present & future conduct ensure future interest & Friendship — rumored party Indian Prisoners & quantity Goods sent Fort Vincenne Fort Knox — thing official respecting — good enough Sir present Complements Doc t Brown — altho unacquainted Family thank present best respects — Adieu dear Sir, believe highest Sentiments Friendship Gratitude, Respect & Esteem— Ob t Serv t . J. S Harris Samuel Hodgdon Esq r Philadelphia

t: Disease, Indian Raids, and Lack of Supplies
s: Wayne reports a number of unfortunate occurances including many deaths at the hands of marauding well-supplied Indians, illness in a number of soldier
c: 10 Major GenlSuperscript text Knox Secy War Pittsburgh 3d Augt. 1792 Sir, honor enclosing copies two letters Mr. Rosecrantz 19th ultimo, one Capt Cass 27th; addition accounts express arrived last evening Fort Washington, GenSuperscript textl. Wilkinson informs loss serjeant, corporal fourteen men, cutting & curing hay, vicinity Fort Jefferson, party nearly one hundred Indians 25th June: & 7th July canoe ascending river, neighbouring settlement Columbia, fired upon party Savages within 3 miles Fort Washington, one man killed another dangerously wounded & boy, son Genl. Spencer taken prisoner: affairs fully informed period, Genl. Wilkinson informs tells me, dispatched express land, letters dated 6th & 9th July, copies transmitted 12th time recurrence happened. account St. Vincents, Mr. Vigo murder flag, corroborated mentioned Rosecrantz's Letter, brought Indian Detroit - officer probability Major Trueman; Colo. Harding informed wore plain coat rather hunting shirt. idea mentioned Genl. Wilkinson letter 6th July "that tribe engaged war, & recently supplied clothing whiteness Shirts", corroborated man taken prisoner Indians, course last summer County Washington, & lately liberated Detroit, place left time June, & arrived Washington Monday last, examined Lieutt County & says seven weeks since - early June upwards one hundred canoes, came way Lake Huron Detroit (now head quarters) 800 Indians i. e. eight canoe; Indians supply'd Detroit clothing, arms, ammunition & provision abundance, immediately proceeded join hostile Indians, mouth Miami [illegible] river Lake Erie. seen man yet, informed Gentleman veracity present examination, told story strait & particular. report massacre Colo Harding Major Trueman, recently Freeman & Frenchman, true & really believe fear true indicates vindictive spirit savages, generally revere flag - things passed by? stamp disgrace upon American character, eye world, enormities permitted impunity? reports - bear strong marks authenticity, leave little ground hope honorable lasting peace; event war, heaven'sÂ ! Savages shall experience keenest effects! Inclosed general monthly return troops place; together copies General Orders upon Courts martial Captn Shaylor Captn John Platt - information two small parties recruits being near - twelve complete suits clothing place; information being actually road: - independent two hundred & eighty five suits Captn Thos Lewis's, Howell Lewis's Wm Preston's companies - nearly sixty Springers ninety five Spark's clothed. Capt. Sparks here yesterday says nearly complete. ordered Majr Clark muster & march men post soonest possible & expect course ten days, four hundred forty suits wanting five companies: really feel uneasy upon business - troops ordered point pleasant probably obliged wait there, time, unpleasant situation; addition necessary present appearances reinforce Genl Wilkinson riflemen, order enable procure forage Fort Jefferson, object first consequence: dismounted Dragoons arrive, immediately forward him, & direct order Horse convenient & safe place Kentucky side river, ready mounting; hope arms, & Horse equipments forwarded however reprehensible conduct respecting transportation stores &c: many Essential articles mentioned invoice 1st January, until 30th June 1792 arrived; & single article contained 1st 17th July - cause? Whilst writing honored your's 27th ulto. enclosures - among copy your's 23d No.8 original arrived. mention letter's & Express Genl Wilkinson 6th & 9th interesting intelligence Major Hamtramck, liberty inclose copies sent Genl Wilkinson, lest accident happened express; impracticable copied time post - pray return copies, convenient. number sick hospital; last detachment brought another malady, besides small pox many men afflicted virulent veneri - every precaution taken prevent spreading; & mean say men moderate stoppages contracted malady, appropriated support & comfort children army - duty severe one Physician - Doctor Carmichael Surgeon belonging army post single one come forward, late appointments - do, good order Dozen Medicine & Medicinal Stores & much wanting post. clothing riflemen being, now, ordered Phila almost tempted direct one hundred mounted rifle volunteers Kentucky, order insure cutting & securing forage Fort Jefferson - next information Mr. Rosecrantz unfavourable, shall adopt measure. honor Sir, obedt & Huml Servt. c: Major Genl Knox Secy War Pittsburgh 24th Augt 1792 Sir Previously entering detail plan operations against hostile indians beg leave offer general observations think war progress. savages become confident, haughty insolent reiterated success, - recently evinced wanton & deliberate massacre flags: enormity can't suffered pass impunity - unless United States America sacrifice national character & justice idle prejudice - & mean oeconomy - order patch temporary peace, neither honorable, expedient, permanent present circumstances impressions; particularly whilst British possession posts Lakes tho directly, convinced do, indirectly stimulate savages continue war: sophistry British Embassadors, agents State spies convince contrary. - until surrender posts, especially seeing & reading deliberate attention treaty held indians, part Five nations time last year Lord Dorchester, acknowledge kind peaceable idea held savages - toward America, sophistical insidious excess: however part Lordships language plain & decisive. - think effect "When King Father granted independance America marked imaginary boundary Great Britain United States, far related themselves place America comply certain conditions: never granted one foot lands; Americans, power right single inch without consent even treaty fully complied part America, not, posts given until every thing fully complied with. King father never forget you: ordered care - General Clerk, leave command orders - Prince Edward Son King father lately arrived chosen band warriors - second command & care you." language Sir, British viceroy, held hostile indians residing in, inhabiting Country, within acknoledged limits United States, August 1791, conclusive evidence, dont actually encourage indians continue war - promise protect them. thus narrative minute - order shew reason think war progress - time shew can't agree opinion General Putnam, ought carry part operations way Lake Erie. believe British avidity, avail themselves pretext assist savages openly. - events prevent us navigating water long hold possession posts: otherwise certainly decidedly favor combined operation water Presque Isle land Fort Washington, Jefferson & Ca - proper time shew prefer route way Presque Isle could advance strong & conclusive reasons favour route preference way big Beaver Cahahoga rivers - being question present liberty offer reasons against fall campaign - especially immediately ensuing. shall pressed time deficient point numbers, discipline manoeuvre - because, ought risk another defeat raw troops: reasonably expected us, present circumstances, endeavour protect frontiers, raise, disciple manoeuvre troops manner suited service intended. - business without exertion & care, require fall & winter effect - let's hindrance's thrown way prevent sufficient force raised time offensive operation (both Congress) known need comment, facts considerations sufficient shew fall proper time active campaign; altho' one two desultory expeditions composed mounted volunteers useful attended success - another time. consider indian - enemy formidable choice time & ground fall year he's strong, - ferocious full Spirits - corn plenty & venison & game every met - Spring - half starved - weak & dispirited - season enterprise upon - strike least expected (hitherto attempted fall year) - timid, disconcerted, & longer formidable. Permit choose season operation - give time manoeuvre & discipline troops, inspire confidence prowess - conduct bravery officer's - Let component parts Legion perfected agreeably Establishment: authorise direct ample & proper magazines forage, stores, provisions thrown advanced posts convenient periods, Fort Washington Fort Jefferson: establish suitable magazines forage & provision Big Beaver place & Fort Washington. - propose two strong desultory parties, comprised mounted volunteer's/ & pleased find avidity kind service / one against Sandusky - /which abandoned mentioned Capt Brant) against indians removed Miami villages St. Josephs river, recent accounts several towns hostile indians expeditions place soon grass Praire's, answer pasture & until every thing readiness forward move Legion Fort Jefferson point operating army previously assemble. movements probably crowned brilliant success; effect distract savage councils - & create jealously safety women & children whilst Legion advancing employed erecting small intermediate Forts proper convenient distances Fort Jefferson point intended establishing strong & permanent post - invariable rule hault early day & secure camp evening temporary breastworks & abbatis cover troops enable repel every kind attack Savages; secure baggage & stores part army - opening offer strike Enemy Light Corps Legion whilst mediating attack upon us. - Give authority arrangements, & pledge reputation officer establish myself Miami villages (or place Miami river thought proper) - face savages wilderness brought against - latter end next July: season indians can't continue together large numbers length time (unless supported British) collect force & approach within striking distances night, view surprising - attacking morning, - Indians, guides, scouts, spies, & Dragoons (who always patrole & hover wide round me) suffer savages advance covered, wait attack - contrary shall feel effects nocturnal charge - & know experience, contemptible enemy night. - convinced expence attending operations great & probably objected to: convinced end, found economical plan, plan adopted insure success. difficulty impracticability procuring & depositing sufficient magazines forage, provision &ca Fort Jefferson large number Cavalry length time likewise offered strong objection. obviate objections beg leave observe part Atlantic middle States, Cavalry supported, better cheaper place Fort Washington. believe demonstrated Horse fed twelve quarts oats eight quarts corn & twenty weight good hay moderate rate twelve thirteen pence per diem - Big Bever - points mounted volunteers assemble; c: [No 29. Maj. Gen Knox.] War department 1 December 1792. Whatever terms offered, persuaded none agreed shall tend sacrifice national character United States. although ardent & growing desire mass Citizens United States peace re-established frontiers, concluded certainty, ignominiously submit peace, unless justice bases — treaty agreed probable, Indians opportunity judging moderation & humanity United States. Correspondence Contractors considered, result transmitted you. materials reparation Soldiers clothing long ordered forwarded suppose ought arrived Pittsburg. Clothing deserters delayed mentioned letter 24 th ulto. way, wit. One hundred Suits — considerable quantity levy clothing Carlisle hand, perhaps answer purpose Deserters & others lost clothing — Clothing next year contracted upon approbation thereof & delivered inspection, conceive Clothing next Year duly furnished. clearly understood, Ground taken Posts established Indian Country advanced Fort Jefferson interim, time & time fixed upon treating — conduct part however advantageous, could justified principles good faith therefore attempted — & money soon go forward. Richmond detachment soon you. Capt. Brock, see papers arrived. recruits Eastward ordered hope receive one detachment one hundred & twenty winter sets in. c: Mouth Detroit River 12th Aug' 1793 Sir, waiting here twelve days reply last answer Indian Nations assembled Rapids Miami. think sufficient reason delay, therefore measures obtain reply, ascertain whether ought longer expect it. purpose judge proper proceed ourselves Miami bay river, necessary communications Indians easy expeditious; time business mission brought issue. therefore request prepared sail tomorrow morning, propose embark. Sir &c B: Lincoln, B: Randolph, T: Pickering. } Commissioners Captain Henry Ford....Commanding Dunmore } Captain Ford having read letter came informed Commissioners, instructed attend Commissioners, receive orders Captain Bunbury; desired us speak him. spoke Captain Bunbury, told Governor Simcoe assigned Dunmore, Captain Ford use Commissioners, Governor Secretary repeatedly right conclude direction go thought proper purpose treaty, except Detroit. orders Governor Simcoe, orders could consent Commissioners deputation them, go Miami bay, river, until Colonel McKee give notice Indians ready receive them. says Commissioners choose go Sandusky, order Dunmore proceed thither. read broken passages Governor Simcoe's letter him. Commissioners asked give extract letter containing orders. answered Mr. Storer might extract. retired together, Captain Bunbury read, Mr. Storer wrote down mouth following words, extract letter Colonel Simcoe Captain Bunbury dated Navy Hall 28d June 1793 "the directing Kings Vessel Carry (the Commissioners) thither anchor therefore conveniently possible Northern shore river, bank purpose remain until hear Colonel McKee. Indians wish visit opposite shore." Detroit River 12th August 1793. above extract day verbally given Captain Bunbury, tho' desired, refuses sign it. Chas. Storer. Tuesday 13th August 1793. Being thus prevented proceeding Miami bay, Commissioners concluded send Message Indian Nations Rapids, letter Colonel McKee. message letter here follow. Chiefs, Warriors Indian Nations assembled foot Rapids Miami River. Brothers.It fifteen days since delivered speech deputies place, explicitly answered written question presented you, gave reasons could Ohio boundary United States. mentioned heads engagements willing behalf United States. particulars together stipulations benefit, judged proper reserve, explained full Council, meet face face. c: Head Treaty King Spain Creek, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Cherokee Indians. Dated Walnut Hills October 28th 1793. Containing 19 Articles. Indians promise ratify former Treaties Spain. Cherokees req request King Spain protection; grants them. nations form alliance, Affective Defensive Catholic Majesty, enter War, without consent king. - Natives agree defend catholic majestys Dominion Louisiana Floridas. Nations request Catholic Majesty settle boundary United States. Catholic majesty agrees settle boundary, protect land. Catholic majesty agrees give annual presents Nations. Chickasaw receive presents Banks Missipippi - Creek Cherokee, Consecold. Choctaws Tom Bigby. Alabamas Mobille elswhere. matters settled Spanish Commisaries Nations respectively - talks delivered them, Nation. shall respect Commisaries, receive governed advice. shall Judge determine business White People. White People families considered Indians, don't apply themselves industry turned Nation. Finally Spanish Nation Indian Nations agree solemnly ratify treaty, consider Spanish King sole Emperor Indians. Catholic Majesty agrees protect them. Spanish Treaty Indians. Yazon 28th October 1793. t: The Sad Affair of Capt. Big Tree of the Seneca
s: Captain Big Tree, the Seneca chief, has committed suicide for unknown reasons; mentions that he was a companion of Cornplanter and New Arrow.  Records
c: [Nº 72. Maj r Gen l Knox Sec y war. —] Head Quarters Greenville 25. Jan y 1794 Sir, lament unfortunate death Captain Big tree, Seneca War Chief, put period existence 23 d instant 3 o'clock P.M. possible cause assigned act suicide, disturbed imagination, conspicuous certain intervals considerable length time. — latter end march last Legion Ville company Corn Planter & Arrow two famous Chiefs tribe, message Six Nations preparatory meeting Grand Council hostile Indians Rapids Miami lake: Corn planter & Arrow delivered message, — Captain Big tree requested liberty speak words concerning matter dwelt heavy upon mind & disturbed rest. "I lost every dear friend — friend heart — General Richard Butler — loved much, heard death, determined act soon follow join him." "But act doing — Great Spirit told wrong — part warrior kill himself, avenge blood friend killing enemies: — solemn vow Great Spirit, sacrifice three hostile Indians manes friend. — part performed vow — killed one Delaware Indian; peace rest until killed two more: Great spirit pleased until completed promise & vow — therefore request let join army, opportunity fulfilling vow — hostile Indians refuse treat." appear vow dwelt upon mind — arrived Head Quarters 3 weeks since, accompanied M r Rosecrants interpreter service U.S.; giving particular narration passed late council hostile Indians — again addressed — "I shall speak sentiments myself & warriors nation & request look full face see mind & heart." "Our warriors desirous doing something, wish opinion & advice upon occasion — Corn planter's Nephew, sends best wishes & lets know ready rise moment desire — many warriors wish join Army; others chose [undecipherable] path stride directly towns parties vicinity command bring Forty strong warriors: — heard Chickasaws join — want [undecipherable] us most. — done — await answer." course day two this, chief Delaware nation arrived flag hostile Indians, requesting appoint time & place settling terms upon peace — message gave visible uneasiness, course evening sallied hut & approached occupied three messengers drawn sword revenge — bad men & come spies — much difficulty could prevailed upon desist, & return hut — however, length apparently reconciled, & invited next morning marquee hear purport message & reply — requested speak words warriors — addressed thus. — Nephews call nephews, always acknowledged us Six Nations uncles. pleased find pride lowered; begin come reason: — proud & mad
