t: French expedition against Spanish Florida
s: Constant Freeman, agent for the Department of War in Georgia, writes Secretary Knox. Discusses certain persons employed in Georgia to recruit a corps
c: Extract letter Constant Freeman, Agent Department War, Georgia, Secretary War, dated Fort Fidius, 18th April, 1794. " long time held suspense different reports circulated, relatively certain persons being employed State, recruit corps troops service France. cannot doubts remaining upon subject. Officers appointed, acting authority French Republic. Parties recruits already marched rendezvous appointed them. Several men corps crossed Oconee, encamped, opposite Greensborough. small party days opposite Rock Landing; since marched Carr's bluff join assembled place. general rendezvous told river St. Mary. agent appointed furnish supplies, purpose received ten thousand dollars. person formerly contractor's clerk post, employed purchase four thousand rations provisions. gone down country execute business. 8th inst. Col. Carr major Williamson came garrison: stayed day night Capt. Martin: officers French legion. confirmed major Williamson shewed Capt. Martin letter instructions received general Clarke, directing repair Fort Phillips, Rock Landing, Carr's Bluff, purpose paying recruits French legion, allowance mileage homes places rendezvous. shewed Capt. Martin list men paid, encamped side Oconee opposite Greensborough, command late Lieut. Bird, captain legion; shewed Capt. Martin saddle bags, told thousand dollars purposes above-mentioned; further informed him, general Clarke cross Oconee ten days time command, Col. Carr one adventurers. Major Williamson employed pedlar. Colonel Carr told me, large detachments marched back Settlements South Carolina State Kentucky. men engaged three months, receive bounties land provinces East West Florida Louisiana, conquer Spaniards. M. Genet appointed major-general, command chief, enquiries taken conciliate Greeks, legion might march country. next day left garrison proceeded journey Carr's bluff. morning soldier deserted Capt. Martin's company, apprehended joined party French legion encamped opposite Rock Landing, Capt. Martin sent message major Williamson, requesting man might returned. received enclosed letter answer, desired give me, might send you. letter confirms above written relatively major Williamson being connected business. many persons named officers corps, rather imprudent mention without evidence fact, forbear feed names. appears Spanish government Florida greatly alarmed preparations making invade precincts, governor East Florida complaint governor State, issued proclamation, dated 6th last month, forbidding persons joining adventures, aiding abetting way whatever. Although fully informed channels above facts, conceive highly proper give further information therein

t: Regarding Kentucky Volunteers, Garrisons, Contractors' Dishonesty, & Plans to Advance
s: Thanks Knox for transmitting the President's commendation. Discusses payment of Kentucky volunteers. Notes troops who will be sent to establish a post
c: N o 76. Maj. Gen. Knox Sec y war. — Head Quarters, Greeneville 7. 1794 Sir, honor acknowledge receipt yours 31st march, several enclosures, including Commission & instructions holding treaty Indian tribes N.W. Ohio, — every part due attention shall paid utmost power & abilities. — Permit Sir, offer gratefull thanks polite manner pleased communicate approbation President United States conduct general since command. — Tomerit approbation great & good man & serve Country effect constant study & highest ambition; fondly hope discipline & prowess troops produce conviction world trust & confidence reposed President honored nomination command American Legion misplaced. — reaches muster & pay rolls mounted Volunteers Kentucky received office; second last muster Fort Washington appear greatest part men enrolled purpose being mustered, Eighty ninety attend, considered officers deserters. therefore decidedly opinion forfeiture pay wise & politic; powerful tendency prevent kind characters desertion future: contrary pass impunity — rewarded receiving full pay time desertion, encourage general dereliction upon occasion perhaps critical & fatal moment. consequence order 31st march directed D.Q.M. General collect sufficient number boats purpose transporting troops & stores [strikethrough: Massac] & appointed major Doyle 4 th Sub Legion command, descend Ohio — immediately select detachment eighty good men — marched hence morning consisting Infantry & matross, ordered furnished ammunition & provision six months. dependence placed enclosed copy letter Governor state Kentucky, dated 10. February last nothing apprehended quarter — force Major Doyle good vigilant officer adequate every purpose. garrisons Forts Steuben & Knox composed invalids selected Legion large totally unfit field & scarcely equal common Garrison duty; mustered, being struck muster & Payrolls respective companies formerly belonged pursuance general order 6. Sept 1793 therefore idea garrisoning post Massac part garrisons question. total number first dont exceed 40. & second fifty men. fact point garrisoning posts river & rear description troops, order advance respectable force possible — aggregate amount two thousand effectives, observe field return honor enclose, together general Return Legion Quarterly returns ordnance, Quartermaster & hospital departments 4 th ultimo. — enclosed copy correspondence Contractors & myself, demonstrate difficulties constantly labored consequence non compliance positive, pressing oft repeated orders providing constant & plentiful supply provision support troops every direction, particularly head line. — appear letter 2 d . instant 200000 rations Cattle, (which informed 25. Provided, person shall hereafter wilfully obstruct, attempt obstruct execution laws United States, wise aiding abetting therein, shall entitled benefit advantage pardon herein granted: provided also. nothing herein contained, shall extend, construed extend remission mitigation forfeiture penalty incurred reason infractions of, obstructions to, laws United States collecting revenue upon distilled Spirits Stills. Allow me, Sir, state matter clearly you, Danger Women & Children ever leave them, obliged remain home plant Corn. period great distance [undecipherable] us hope, approved place holding Grand Council. ill disposed Indians advantage perhaps Perhaps destroy Women & Children. know Hearts Savage desperate barbarous particularly supported case [illegible]. call upon you, Sir, name Wyandots & Delawares protection. t: [Copy] Talk from the Choctaw Nation to the Creek Nation
s: Friendship between nations of Indians after peace talk and smoking of tobacco.  Noted conspiracy of Americans selling land and Indian people.  Propose
c: /copy/ Chactaw Creek Nation June 10th 1795 5 June 10 + 224 following Kings, Headmen & warriors Chactaw Nation, assembled, send Talk elder brother, Mad Dog Tuckabatches, White Lieutenant Oakfuskeys, Nine Hadgo [i.e., Hadjo] Abecuckies Apoyl Hickory Ground, elder brothers Creeks general, upper lower Towns. [Blotted: Friends] Brothers. received Talk — Governor orleans forwarded us together beads tobacco smoaked, having met head men Nation opportunity tell so. — tell brightened Chain friendship — hold fast hand remember times buried Hatchet hope never dug again. Brothers! makes hearts sorrowful see elder brothers Chickasaws embroiled war, whilst [line-ending stroke] much better employed hunting planting families— father us red people desired us live peace, instead following advice, bad Council kill [blot] one another. Brothers, listen Talks, us ashamed throwing away, — peace Chickasaws once before, wish — send white beads opportunity, named one beloved men Taboca carry Talk Chickasaws advise kill red men, peace. know sorry [blot:what] did, Talks, hope also. Therefore peace spill blood. _ Give us answer send father Commandan[t] Mobile soon possible. Brothers, father orleans told us [the] Americans sold us lands. so, continue united never us, kill one another, wil[l] left defend them? thought o[f] things, remember good advice father[s] Spaniards give us every day— speak always good red people, ar[e] children; promised us ammunition guns defend ourselves [line-ending stroke] attacked. nothing say, 224 beg again advice, send peace Talks place Chickasaws, receive white beads token everlasting peace us — smoake tobacco sent you, send Talk brothers Cherokees peace also. t: Provisions and Transportation
s: Sent beef cattle to Presque Isle, noted boats should be built to transport provisions.  Saw mill neglected at Buffalo Creek and could not be repaired
c: 321 Pittsburg 15 November 1795 Sir received letter 7th inst fourth [undecipherable] 10th instant. sent forward Presqu'isle forty beef cattle added Provision previously sent forward form supply intended Garrison Presqu'isle & Le BÅuf first April 1796 except Article forage working Oxen Viz. Corn -- boat load endeavouring send forward presume necessary proper boat boats built Presqu'isle transportation forage &ca Cataragarus & Buffalo Creek doubt sufficient quantity being obtained reasonable rate -- unfortunate Circumstance Saw Mill race & dam place neglected until became late complete Winter otherwise Plant &ca above purpose buildings might provided due season Several Militia dragoon horses occasionally taken carry baggage &ca parties March Presqu'isle frequently carry baggage escorts Provision & stores &ca, several excessive fatigue & want full supply forage far reduced able return & therefore died, others limbs broken almost impassable road Cossawaga Presqu'isle unavoidably perished previously horses being employed above service appraised competent Judges -- apprehensive might killed fall 322 [undecipherable] hands. shall communicate part letter respecting dragoon horses Colo Butler & guided opinion. enclosed herewith General return stores post first October since hospital stores & Medicines received & destined Head Quarters sent forward pursuaded application ought Legislature Pennsylvania opening road Fort Franklin Presqu'isle & improving navigation French Creek. Road Pittsburg Fort Franklin great utility great respect Sir obedient Humble Servant Isaac Craig Honble Timothy Pickering Seretary War Philadelphia

t: Report Regarding Suspected Traitors
s: Wayne relates to McHenry the movements of Thomas Powers and Victor de Collot, two enemy agents operating in the Northwest Territory, and tells of his
c: (Private) 5 [Marginalia] 7-8-1796 [/Marginalia] Head Quarters Fort Washington 18th July 1796 Sir arrived place 5th Instant & found man Powers G Wilkinson Greenville several days, returned & descended Ohio 20th ultimo rapids, probably delayed week more,he shewed certain instructions General Wilkinson put suit interrogatories, certain Newman, & answer'd satisfaction, reward Powers One Thousand Dollars, either person Nwman, Powers number callers Wilkinson & gave object visiting Greenville obtain materials writing history country: &ca 29th ultimo De Collot &ca came across land & Lexington place, immediately waited upon Mr Commandant, inquired find G- W- informed marched Greenville days since rapids Miami, & uncertain was: De Collot, appeared greatly disappointed & wanted much interview great & popular General, certainty overtaking follow, great number letters him, wished present hands, present content himself enclosing them, & requests forwarded immediate & safe express & De Collot proceed rapids occasion wait week ten days; large packet placed hands Commandant DeCollot early next morning addressed G - W - reiterated injunctions dispatch & safety. De Collot immediately descended river & met side rapids, Colo St. Clair (who appointed Command Militia Prothonotary Illinois Country Govr St. Clair) moments conversation DeCollot wait rapids several days, order see Country & transact business consequence probably accompany St Clair Illinois; knowing character St Clair & circumstances, think prudent confidential communications respecting De Collot: St Clair waited upon behalf inhabitants Kaskaskias Illinois anxious small post Quarter troops supported produce country certainty, & moderate terms, place; post place happy effect & give energy [New laws?] & respectability Government Spaniards Quarter imposing improper ideas minds people & impressing apathy & imbecility United States. requested give particular statement writing upon subject matter upon speaking promised soon returned country. ready descend river, cargo merchandise & probable accompanied De Collot. intention land Massaca & proceed horseback Kaskaskias & send boat round Mississippi, expected DeCollot accompany & boat go round place. communicated complaint against Capt Pike supposed insult offered Spanish flag, & act writing officer demanding true state facts relative subject. Mr. St Clair heard complaint, & Capt. Pike done duty - insult offered Spanish Officer attempting pass post; requested obliging charge letter Pike & printed Acts Congress carrying effect Treaty Spain &Ca assure Spaniards friendly disposition Government towards Nation; dispatches ready half hour, & embraced opportunity enclose packet private note Capt Pike copy transmitted. addition shall immediately give orders Capt Pasteur Commandant Fort Knox: Similar forward Capt Taylor Capt Pike, trust, nefarious machinations enemies Country, fully discover'd & prime movers receive punishment due demerits; wishes sentiments honor Obt Huml Sert Anty Wayne Honble James McHenry Esqr Secy War [Right margin] No. 7 18 July 1796 Gen Wayne Sec McHenry

c: Doctor Charles Brown November 11th--1797 Recd 9th March 98 165 Received State Dep't. Nov. 24. 1894. R.P.O.401810 Received State Dep't. Nov. 24. 1894. R.P.O.401810 D'Etroit Novr. 11th. 1797 Dr. Sir sorrow yellow fever again given cause alarm cityzens Philada. hope seriou report makes it-- bad newes Mrs Hodgdon hope give much uneasynys me, elegant fox skines provided fer unfortunately lost thro depredation moth per- -served it, fur Merchants say suffered severely season account but, hope Mis Hodgdon think accadent happned thro neglect, beg leav assure engaged & shall care sharpest teethed moth shall able injure Part inclosed account paid long ago death Genl. Wayne whose request first undertook duty attending Indians promis ten dollers pr. month extra pay fer servece 150 dollers extra attendanes during treaty Green Ville extreordonary fatigue heat weather nearely finished me. Genrl. Wilkinson recemends five dollars pr. month & account accordingly although acknowledges servecis intitle more, adding Indean cost country great deal, & concludes honour thing--The yellow boys refuse attended Doctor & patients distance five hundred miles, genl. supposes money paid sight having wrote back account pray received money appropriate formerly-- Indean polite believ share cause kindness often troublesom, N.I nothing fear ^at present think keep larger fores amongst owing belive Genl wishes keep country. Dr. Sir obdt humble Servt Chas. Brown Col. Hodgdon

c: Bellfield Talbot County Aug 12th 1798 dear Sir Inclosed Letter received young Man Neighborhood wishes Commission Army much Knowledge Him. thought best send Letter, enabled judge Fitness Office - Since Return Mr. William Swan Easton recommended Philadelphia Doct: Coates, Col: Nicols, whose letters left Me, anxious know Fate application, assumes spirited clever young Man, good sense, & probably good Officer; [undecipherable] and, Estimation essential. ~ Mr. Francis Q. Willson young gentleman respectable Family, devious being Trooper, & thankful Commission; brave young Man & good Character, Sensible & highly federal, consistent prior Applications, happy Success. Days Home, went Mr. Perry's Fo Marriage Daughter Mr. William Smith Son Mr. Thomas Smith Kent County, dancing handsom young looking Lady. upon Fan, lame even since & unfortunately deprived Power meaning among Constituents, seems essential I've least Chance success next Election ~ Mr. Seney perpetual Motion, & Friends increasing [undecipherable], innumerable lies Shadow Foundation, Circulation, destroy good Opinion People; Sedition Bill called Gag Law, They[undecipherable] much upon, & fear much Truth, [undecipherable] misrepresentations Law, unfavorable Impressions upon Minds People, impossible remove Time; foresaw voted Bill, & told Congressional Friends Time, Effect probably produce ~ able collect Opinion Seney elected, [undecipherable] Myself Person, Prudence forbids it. ~ soon able go thro District, & endeavor remove unjust Prejudices taken against Sedition Bill - hear Mr. Seney great many Persons riding Day & Night, lying trying poison Minds People, & representing [undecipherable] Enemy ~ Idea Violence & Virulence Jacobins here, & wonderful relate Numbers increasing Beyond Calculation; & Time observed Insolence keeps Pace Devilty French - assured good Friend none decidedly federal [undecipherable] ought appointed Office, present critical &alarming State Affairs: ask Tory during Revolutionary War applied Office, whether application rejected Contempt & pray! Jacobins Day better Friends Government, Tories Independence, certainly Inference leave ~ conclude unnecessarily frightened, wish strongest & safest situation meet worst Enemies. many influential Friends. hear Motion. Mr. Hammond learn combated Mr. Leney last Tuesday Easton, & Friends joy defeated Him, notwithstanding Partizans collected Purpose. see Baltimore Papers Colonel Howard & General Smith [undecipherable], much pleased [undecipherable] Colonel defeat General ~ delighted see Senator come strong & decided. best Respects Friend Stoddert, presume going surmoningly ~ I, Accountant Navy Department [undecipherable, Office. mentioned Friend [undecipherable] appointment greatly disapproved Federalists here, flatter myself Appointment good & told confess Risque it. late jacobinical Promotions [undecipherable] here, Colonel Benson general, recently publicly Easton, [undecipherable] Jefferson President, War Eve War France ~ meaning Doubt thereby war [undecipherable] Mr. Adams. Mr. William Hayward Colonel, long deemed jacobinical. lately conversed & find changing & think votes all, vote Me. Colonel Samuel Wright commands another Regiment & [undecipherable], bitter French Jacobin: see Reliance placed upon militia here. [undecipherable] Adieu! sincerely Sr W. Hindman

c: Philadelphia 25th January 1799. Sir 17th January 1798 agreeable instructions wrote Barnard Hudson & informed determination discontinue Port Fort Ranselaer, time pointed method closing concerns respecting business date wrote Michael Houden Store keeper Albany arrangement Mr. Houden securing stores: letter duly received, answered. Difficulties respect transportation Ordnance & heavy Stores urged account season year. subject again wrote Mr. Hudson 14th February, & communicated fully directions Subject, since time untill 2d instant, heard nothing further business. seems however removal taken place & stores remained care Mr. Hudson usual, trust think ought remain care until complied orders given respecting them, time naturally come forward shew reason earlier attended & urge claim compensation safe keeping. certainly abandon Stores & base charge person insure total loss every thing capable being taken away. think best renew order delivery Stores first directed present claims compensation submitted. Sir &c Samuel Hodgdon Jas. McHenry Esqr Secretary War

Alexandria, ? Leeburgh head quarters Rendezvous. first (comparatively) large & populous, & Navigation, -- 40 miles above navigation, & small village -- unhealthy, supplied provisions &c.a --3.d Prince William Fauquier ought annexed, instead Prince William & Loudoun, join extreme corners only. Dumfries Prince William, Fauquier Court H.o might Rendezvous. first Navigation; latter 40 miles above, & central. -- 4.th York Town centre 6.th subdivision Williamsburgh; & 5th, Northumberland Court House low 9.th subdivision; either Westmoreland Richmond Court Houses point centrality, eligable. t: Efforts to Deal with Cherokees and Horse Thievery
s: Refers to the many serious complications in Cumberland with the Cherokees stealing horses. Sent Zackfield Maclin to the Cherokees and to the Creeks to
c: Knoxville June 5th 1799 Sir many serious complaints people Cumberland, travellers Country (Cherokees particular) Stealing Horses induced send Mr. Zuekfield Maclin 19th March (a person service MrHawkins) nation, Creeks prevent fulre injuries kind, collect many Horses could stolen view restore owners Copy instructions answer, Report number Horses found defferent Towns, puncissaly information knowledge, being eye witness neighbors, enclose, returned unfortunately without bringing one Horses tho expense going considerable, Chiefs Confessed thefts comitted people, councils exertions promised recover them. further information gained, Horses taken Georgia else where, believe ever returned. [51] [editor's note: last number brackets appears pencil] Stealing Horses cause much evil differently, seems Chief complaint People against Indians. complaint against people, Horses delivered Indians, difficulty kept, soon let Range, even field many stolen Whites, often Indians bring them, hardly used, expence keeping months greater Caleu apart Indian Business gives trouble rest, know proceed advise remedy it.. opinion, justice due people, lost Horses, induce Government stop Annuity being dirlered, part till Stolen property returned, measure Government, convence people Complaints time attended to, believe good effect upon minds Indians, submit oppinion Judgement. received last post packet adressed him, Officer Commanding absence, - letter John McKee esquire, Officers Natchez Territory Cover. forwarded George Dryer General's Express - delained days Arrival Mail, went water Sunday 2nd Instant. receive conveyance Return Quarter Master shores delivered month May. Col Butler being place - suppose shall shall arrangements directed delivering Stores quarterly hay yearly. Respectfully yr Humb Sert David Henley Agent War honorable James M Henry

t: Complaints Lodged Against White
s: White cited his motivation as gaining recruits not personal gain for allegations of recruiting men while intoxicated.  Detailed account of incident.
c: Philadelphia July 2d 1799 Sir, Secretary War yesterday informed complaints against recruiting Officer lodged him, two young men names Waller & Lauk. done anything even appear wrong, great anxiety promotion recruiting service, prospects gain, circumstances require it, proud temper above it. allegations against could understand Secretary enlisted Waller & Lauk intoxicated, taken bond one hundred Dollars discharge - first charge..They enlisted Second Lieutenant, 'tho know perfectly sober; enlisted early day, several times morning talking subject. Justice swore respectable man, certificate subject - second charge - day Brigade meeting County Sussex, Waller & Lauk enlisted, came collect Recruits, march Dover; found two absented themselves. called next day informed resided search them; found. went Dover, four days afterwards recruiting Sergeant left Sussex came up, informed me, Waller & Lauk wished - offered eighty one hundred Dollars off; swore die rather go army. extremely loss proceed - unacquainted business myself consulted several respectable characters Dover, advised nearly raised company, discharge them, condition furnish two three substitutes pay money enough procure - practice during former war, four years past Capt. Wells recruiting Western army Dover done - could find authority given discharge person sworn, determined pursue another tact - accordingly wrote note, order induce come Dover, held idea might possibly discharged terms therein mentioned. effect, accordingly came Dover. hopes persuading stay, used every argument power, purpose. saw impossible detain without keeping constantly guard; unprepared, having arms guard house - great object manage away present leaving Country, holding idea being perhaps discharged, (on form[undecipherable]) until could write Colonel, (which intended place) know power discharging them, until company ordered march; time (having suspicions) might easily taken. - believe given bonds sum discharged, told question time - however bond W. Cardwell Second Lieutenant myself provided W. Hazzard (a juror enlisted, found deaf serve) enter them. considered best security against desertion; 'tho told so; business managed discharged order keep spirits hand. Mr. Hazzard lived neighbourhood, intimate them. supposed enterey bond induce keep watch them. could possible prospect recovering money knew age (neither believe nineteen years old) consequently Instrument void. conduct recruiting Officer know given universal satisfaction, produce respectable testimony Delaware. W. Mr.[undecipherable] believe present business managed understood it. Having left Bar flattering prospects enter army motives worthy American, - having used indefatigable exertions recruiting business, enlist fifty sixty men six weeks, spend one hundred eighty Dollars, never expected returned conscious purity intentions feel Sir, keenest - sensibility attempt injure me. author little doubt certain democratic Lawyer County Sussex. m brightest ambition best first raised Company twelve Regiments accomplish desirable object, ready entered service pecuniary sacrifice. taken liberty submit candid, hasty statement, least suspicions might moment rest conduct. shall return tomorrow Dover shall extremely anxious hear business interesting Gentleman Officer. obedt. & humble Servt. Saml White [undecipherable strike-through] Genl Hamilton

t: Secretary of the State's Opinion Regarding Presidential Power Over Officers' Commissions, Relative to the Court Martial of Richard Hunt
s: Pickering submits his observations concerning the question of presidential power in officer's commissions and of the propriety of Sgt. Richard Hunt's
c: Department State. July 9th 1799 Sir, letter 29 Ult inclosing proceedings Court Martial case Richard Hunt, Sergeant Corps Artillerists Engineers considered two questions concerning Opinions Heads departments required President, observe. 1. appointment Officer nominated Senate approved appears complete; Commission act President alone, merely evidence appointment; fact evidence establish. 2. crime committed Richard Hunt highly aggravated - desertion being accompanied dangerous kind fraud; therefore sentence death pronounced against ought executed. respectfully Sir Yr. obed servant signed/ Timothy Pickering Copy Secretary War Navy Department 6th July 1799 Sir, considered attentively reference heads Departments, case Sergeant Hunt, sentenced death Court Martial. Officers composed Court, appears, received Commissions, notified appointment, returned office acceptance oath office actually entered upon duty. Commission consider evidence appointment, appointment itself. tho' desireable cases officers enter upon duty, power, producing Commissions, show clearest best evidence authority cannot conceive want evidence, cases authority sufficiently established evidence, vitiate proceedings. know during last war, nothing common officers serve years, sit Courts-Martial, without Commissions. observe proceedings Court first presented you, appear upon face two thirds members concurred required sentence death, 8th article appendix rules articles war, proceedings returned General Hamilton objection stated, caused omission supplied interlination sentence, President Court Judge Advocates added certificate signature two thirds Members concur, words interlined omitted accident, time first signature Sentence. whole proceeding transmission sentence General Hamilton appears illegal. Without entering question whether President Court, having dissolved it, could again assemble it, presence, concurrence whole Court presence prisoner, could alter proceedings, clear understanding President Judge Advocate alone right it. proceedings Court Martial read, believe signed presence Court. admit President Judge Advocate could afterwards alter proceedings subject Fame, liberty, life man two individuals law gives priviledge: sentence first transmitted, sufficient justify execution man, defect [illegible] subsequent proceedings. whether sentence transmitted sufficient, question, opinion, depend upon practice heretofore observed Army similar cases. invariable practice insert sentences sentences death, words "two thirds Court concurring" words effect, omission words present instance vitiate proceedings Court. hand, always practice insert words show two thirds Court concur sentences death, presume point understood Army, sentence death implied concurrence two thirds members. idea wording 8th Section Appendix forcibly impresses mind. opinion then, upon whole case, depends upon matter record office. honor greatest respect Sir, obedt humble servant. (signed) Ben Stoddert Honourable Secretary War

t: Ceremony for General Washington
s: Major Craig describes to Samuel Hodgdon the ceremony in Pittsburgh held to honor General Washington.
c: Public Service Isaac Craig D QM G Samuel Hodgdon Esqr Philadelphia Major Isaac Craig 10 January 1800 Rec'd Draft comes Next Pan 6 1/2 Pittsburgh 10th January 1800 Sir moment favour 3d instant Received. QM Genl says expects set Philadelphia days defer journey longer next Post shall send draft Balance present acct. certainly possible Congress [undecipherable] Army whilst Negotiations pending Court Directory - Wednesday last Military & Citizens Pittsburgh together Uniform Calvary & Infantry companies neighboring county united doing Funeral Honors Memory beloved & Immortal Chief. Every Citizen & Every Solider seemed Vie occasion conform Order President - O Year sorrowful beginning heavy clouds seem hang us trust however Majority Congress determined right - Barrell Coffie kind enough Promise come hand, much wanted. Sir obedient servant Isaac Craig Saml Hodgdon Esqr Philadeia

c: Report Mr. Committee appointed 28th November 1800 prepare bring bill regulating grants land, appropriated refugees British Provinces Canada Nova Scotia. 19th January 1801. Committed committee whole House Wednesday next. Bill reported day. 26th January 1801. Ordered engrossed. [illegible] [illegible] 870 Committee referred report Secretary War, Secretary Comptroller Treasury, subject refugees Canada Nova Scotia. Report 73 persons presented claims entitled relief provisions act April 1798.__That 18 claims disallowed, 6 suspended want sufficient proofs, 49 allowed. four special cases, Secretaries Comptroller recommend allowance 2,000 acres. 45 claimants arranged five classes, allowing first class, five number, 1,000 acres each; second class, fifteen number, 750 acres each; third class, fourteen number, 500 acres each; fourth class, ten number, 250 acres each; claimant fifth class 100 acres; making altogether including special cases 33,500 acres. six suspended cases, allowed, increase quantity land 40,000 acres. Committee considering whole amount claims falls short generally expected; claimants original holders, losses sufferings considerable, greater number many years indigent circumstances, thus reduced, account having joined American cause, waited twenty years compensation, recommend allowed, fourth class half section 320 acres instead 250; others proportion, difference 4,740 acres. particular cases, committee propose two alterations. first relates case L.F. Delesdernier, Nova Scotia refugee, placed third class, rate 500 acres. claim deceased brother John, enlisted army United States, served end war, father mother disallowed. last disallowed "it proved obliged leave Nova Scotia, came hither intent aid United States." Although proper rejected claim want proof, appears account having left Nova Scotia, during war, joining son, lost property, ever since supported son son, (they being past 70 father having deprived senses number years) appeared committee sufficient reason raising son, meritorious useful officer during war, third second class. case heirs James Boyd, whose claim considered Secretaries Comptroller one specific cases, allowed 2,000 acres. Secretaries Comptroller state "James Boyd, lost 50,000 acres land, improvements east side know River St. Croix." One heirs attends business, considering compensation altogether inadequate requested claim included among reported on, rather choosing referred suspended cases next session Congress, time investigate merits. c: Fort Hamilton July 12 1793 James O'Hara Esqr, Qu Mr General Sir Agreeably orders 10 Instant Honble Brigadier Genl James Wilkinson examined & inspected following lots Indian Corn find follows. Vizt. Lott No. 1 containing 1495 bushels estimation considerably damaged, being extremely dirty, being put damp impregnated Sweat Horses, dampness received boxes transported otherwise. Lott No. 2 containing 2960 bushels estimate considerably damag'd causes above stated excepting 635 bushels back lower room, good wants cleaning. Lott No. 3 containing 2625 bushels estimating found tho' much want winnowing consequence much liable damage clean corn. Lott No. 4 containing 860 bushels estimation somewhat damag'd think might perserved tolerable condition clean'd. One Stack hay, containing 19,760 solid feet agreeably extimation 60 Ton good Prairie afford. Altho' Corn damag'd above stated, opinion cleaning early period, keeping cool, chiefly render'd preserv'd fit use. purpose cleaning & preserving above quantity Corn, opinion, ten men necessary Standing Fatigue advantage Wind Fann assistance. t: Unable to Comply With Orders of October 21
s: Williams misunderstood McHenry's orders of October 21. He is reluctant to comply with those orders, as it would prove both expensive and embarrassing.
c: Springfield Novr 15th 1799 Sir find letter 8th instant misapprehended orders 21st ultimo. sorry mistake occasioned trouble produced delay transmitting monies use Armory, compliance orders embarrassing expensive me, acquaintance Seat Government, had, Agency burdensome & Commissions equivalent trouble & responsibility, exceed wages - neither rely upon Draughts favor persons occasionally going Philadelphia,the distance being great, opportunities seldom occur, & traders place confine business purchasing York & Boston - think transact business ease facility, give directions Draughts shall answered Office Discount York - shall wait impatiently until know Pleasure. Sir respectfully obedient servant, Jos. Williams Honble James McHenry Esqr. Springfield Novr 25 1799 Sir, Enclosed Contracts Mr James Byers Jur supply rations Armours - executed agreeable directions, Bondsmen introduced ample Securities Sum ordinary magnitude. utmost respect Sir obedient Servant Jas. Williams Honble James McHenry Esqr.

Every precaution, howeever, shall taken prevent speculations defrauding soldiers. judge best, being short, whether shall permitted return Philadelphia: Col.o Pope attend expect - shall greatest exections dispatch business whit him. public service cannot, detainly, suffer indulgence weeks enable bring family country. know friendship therefore rely second application Secretary War. leave absence granted necessary send trunk papers might miss me. best compliments W. t: In Support of Hodgdon
s: Colesworthy regrets he cannot do more to help Hodgdon but hopes that Congress will decide in his favor.
c: Letter Mr. Colesworthy Dated 12 Decem. 1792 Recd 26 Borton December 12. 1792. Dear Sir esteemed favor 27th November came hand 10 Instant, whilst deeply impressed sense Gratitude instance Friendship & Patronage, regret moment beyond Power render taht Assistance cearnestly whish - believe me, Sir, - willingly coem Aid, reder every Service small Abilities could yield you, could share sho[undecipherable] times mentioned - but, sorry, sorry say present state things, beyond Power. & Sensations feel account means small, sensations Man filled due sense situation, willingly exert every Move Faculty Soul oblige experienced tried Friends. Since arrival Borton, supinely set down hope, Congress yield Redress Merit & Zeal Service United States justly entitle . Sir, Journal, being conceive Statement Facts, idle, already passed inspection many Gentlemen Town, minds enlightened upon subject; believe Assertions, view Singular Report Committee, light ought considered. Brother enjoys health & makes respects family, pleased accept fervent prayers continued happiness. Adieu, dear Sir, sincerly Friend Sam Colesworthy Junr. Samuel Hodgdon, Esquire
